newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says everyone won at Mideast summit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says everyone won at Mideast summit.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Thursday that all sides had won at a Middle East summit this week aimed at halting Israeli-Palestinian clashes in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Christopher also said he was ready to go the Middle East when it might be useful, but had no plans to do so at the moment. There has been speculation he could visit the region at the beginning or end of an Africa tour he is due to start on Monday.

Asked about perceptions by both Israelis and Palestinians that Israel had given away nothing, and the Palestinians gained nothing, at the summit, Christopher said: "I don't think it ought to be evaluated in terms of winners and losers."

Speaking before talks with Tunisian Foreign Minister Habib Ben Yahia, Christopher said that while a week ago Israelis and Palestinians were fighting, now they had agreed to hold talks. "In that sense, everyone comes out a winner," he said.
"But we've got a long way to go. There are difficult times ahead, and I think we need to see some results flowing from those negotiations," he told reporters.

The Washington summit agreed that Israeli and Palestinian officials would meet Sunday at the Erez crossing point between Israel and the Gaza Strip to discuss an Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron. U.S. special Middle East coordinator Dennis Ross will attend.
